## Overview

The `compute` test category collects tests that check Vulkan compute dispatch and compute-shader behavior, including dispatch coordinates, shader-side memory effects, indirect command generation, cooperative matrices, and workgroup-memory rules.

## Background Knowledge

- A compute dispatch divides work into workgroups, and each invocation can observe both its workgroup coordinates and its coordinates within that workgroup. These values determine which result element an invocation should produce and are central to the built-in-variable and basic-dispatch tests.
- Workgroup memory is shared by invocations in one workgroup, while storage-buffer contents persist across dispatches and are visible to later pipeline stages only when the required synchronization establishes ordering and visibility. This distinction is needed for the barrier, indirect-dispatch, zero-initialization, and explicit-layout families.
- Cooperative matrices are distributed matrix values operated on collectively by a subgroup or workgroup. Their scope, dimensions, operand use, and storage layout affect both the generated shader and the reference computation used by the cooperative-matrix tests.

## Category Structure

```text
compute
├── pipeline
├── shader_object_spirv
└── shader_object_binary
```

Each construction-type root receives the same implementation child factories through the dispatcher. `shader_object_spirv` and `shader_object_binary` are non-VulkanSC roots. Individual implementation families can omit cases that their execution model or Amber-based artifacts do not support.

## How the Families Fit Together

The families share compute-dispatch setup and host-side result checking, but isolate different contracts:

- **Dispatch and indexing** covers ordinary shader side effects, large SSBO indexing, device-group dispatch bases, and compute built-ins.
- **Command generation and handoff** covers indirect dispatch commands supplied by the host or generated by a preceding compute shader, including the required compute-to-indirect synchronization.
- **Matrix operations** covers NV and KHR cooperative-matrix use modes, dimensions, layouts, conversions, addressing, and delegated null-constant cases.
- **Workgroup-memory behavior** covers zero initialization and explicit layout, aliasing, padding, size limits, byte copies, and zero-initialization interactions.

The Level-3 pages explain the family-specific parameter dimensions, execution, validation, and failure boundaries. The registration-only dispatcher is represented here rather than as a separate technical page.

## Category Notes

The registration-only [`vktComputeTests.cpp`](../../modules/vulkan/compute/vktComputeTests.cpp#L48-L85) dispatcher creates the three construction-type roots and attaches the child factories. [`vktComputeTestsUtil.cpp`](../../modules/vulkan/compute/vktComputeTestsUtil.cpp#L1) provides shared compute-test infrastructure and has no separate Level-3 page. The `cooperative_matrix` and `workgroup_memory_explicit_layout` families are excluded from Vulkan SC by compile-time guards; their Level-3 pages document further per-family exclusions.
